Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

competitor noun

also competitors, rival, rivals, opponent, contestant, opponent (for office)

classical

Cic. Off. 1.38; Cic. Att. 1.1.1 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 44, 179
M-O s.v. competitor

competītor, competītōris m.

noun, third declension

a rival, a competitor

In Cicero above all a rival candidate for office; Lewis & Short gives it for rivals in general, and Traupman and Morgan–Owens for a competitor in a game or in business. A woman is competītrīx (Cic. Mur. 40).

Other words

  • aemulus, aemulī m. — a rival, one who tries to equal or outdo another

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Marc. 1: aemulus atque imitātor (Lewis & Short)

    As an adjective, emulous, rivalling; in a bad sense, jealous (Lewis & Short).

  • adversārius, adversāriī m. — an opponent (in a contest, a game or a lawsuit)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. App. 13.3; Traupman 179

    Lewis & Short: an opponent in any contest, “in which the contending parties may be the best friends”.

Examples

  • victōrem forte gymnicī certāminis jactantiōrem cum vīdisset Phryx sophus, interrogāvit an plūs adversārius valuisset ejus.

    When the Phrygian sage happened to see the winner of an athletic contest boasting rather much, he asked whether his opponent had been the stronger.Phaedr. App. 13.1–4

See also competition, competition.
